name: Pick and place
note: Stage 1: a recorded run of the Task agent where one had every field right, else a written reference dialogue (task_mode). Stage 2: a recorded run of the Layout agent (layout.run). Stage 3: coordination numbers from studio/data (final RobotATC campaign).
note_ko: 페이지용 대본 리플레이. 사용자 발화는 연구자가 쓴 것(reference replay)이고 사용자 연구 기록이 아님. 설비·검사·조율 수치는 studio/data (RobotATC 캠페인 7, 집기–놓기 프로그램)에서 옴.

chat.text: We want a robot to move parts from a conveyor onto a bench. A part weighs 1 kg. The line has to handle 1800 parts an hour, and the robot does nothing else in the cycle.
chat.text_ko: 컨베이어의 부품을 작업대로 옮길 로봇이 필요합니다. 부품은 1 kg 입니다. 시간당 1800개를 처리해야 하고, 로봇은 이 일만 합니다.

chat.text:
textbook search: robot work type pick and place conveyor bench part 1 kg 1800 parts per hour
passages from pp. 225, 239, 218, 239, 224, 307
chat.text_ko:
교재 검색: robot work type pick and place conveyor bench part 1 kg 1800 parts per hour
찾은 구절의 쪽: 225, 239, 218, 239, 224, 307

chat.text: I propose that this job is a pick‑and‑place operation, which is the textbook term for moving parts from one location to another. The engineer said the robot will pick parts from a conveyor and place them on a bench. Does that sound right to you? (p. 218)
chat.text_ko: I propose that this job is a pick‑and‑place operation, which is the textbook term for moving parts from one location to another. The engineer said the robot will pick parts from a conveyor and place them on a bench. Does that sound right to you? (p. 218)

chat.text: Yes, that is right.
chat.text_ko: Yes, that is right.

chat.text: I see that the robot will pick a part from the conveyor and place it on a bench. That means we have two points: P1 is the conveyor pick point, and P2 is the bench place point. The carrying move is from P1 to P2. So the program would be [[1, 2]]. Is that correct? (p. 218)
chat.text_ko: I see that the robot will pick a part from the conveyor and place it on a bench. That means we have two points: P1 is the conveyor pick point, and P2 is the bench place point. The carrying move is from P1 to P2. So the program would be [[1, 2]]. Is that correct? (p. 218)

chat.text: Yes, that is right.
chat.text_ko: Yes, that is right.

chat.text: Which gripper will the robot use, and what is its mass in kilograms?
chat.text_ko: Which gripper will the robot use, and what is its mass in kilograms?

chat.text: A standard two-finger gripper of the robot vendor, 0.5 kg.
chat.text_ko: A standard two-finger gripper of the robot vendor, 0.5 kg.

chat.text: The payload is the sum of the heaviest part and the gripper. The part is 1 kg and the gripper is 0.5 kg, so the payload is 1.5 kg. The textbook does not give the part weight, but we use the engineer’s value. (p. 218)
chat.text_ko: The payload is the sum of the heaviest part and the gripper. The part is 1 kg and the gripper is 0.5 kg, so the payload is 1.5 kg. The textbook does not give the part weight, but we use the engineer’s value. (p. 218)

chat.text: Yes, that is right.
chat.text_ko: Yes, that is right.

chat.text:
textbook search: production rate 1800 parts per hour cycle time 2 sec robot pick place
passages from pp. 225, 239, 495, 495, 239, 226
chat.text_ko:
교재 검색: production rate 1800 parts per hour cycle time 2 sec robot pick place
찾은 구절의 쪽: 225, 239, 495, 495, 239, 226

chat.text:
Cycle time: 3600 s per hour ÷ 1800 parts per hour = 2.0 s per part (2 s). (p. 225)
Machine or station time: none – the robot does nothing else in the cycle.
Moves in one cycle: 1 carrying move (P1→P2) + 1 empty move back to P1 = 2 moves.
Time per move: 2.0 s ÷ 2 moves = 1.0 s per move. (p. 225)
chat.text_ko:
Cycle time: 3600 s per hour ÷ 1800 parts per hour = 2.0 s per part (2 s). (p. 225)
Machine or station time: none – the robot does nothing else in the cycle.
Moves in one cycle: 1 carrying move (P1→P2) + 1 empty move back to P1 = 2 moves.
Time per move: 2.0 s ÷ 2 moves = 1.0 s per move. (p. 225)

chat.text: Yes, that is right.
chat.text_ko: Yes, that is right.

chat.text: For the conveyor pick point (P1), is the robot entering from above the conveyor or from the side? For the bench place point (P2), is the robot entering from above the bench or from the side? The robot will use an approach move to each point and a depart move from it.
chat.text_ko: For the conveyor pick point (P1), is the robot entering from above the conveyor or from the side? For the bench place point (P2), is the robot entering from above the bench or from the side? The robot will use an approach move to each point and a depart move from it.

chat.text: From above at both.
chat.text_ko: From above at both.

chat.text:
Here is the full specification:
The work type is a pick‑and‑place operation.
The program is [[1, 2]]: pick from point 1 (conveyor) and place at point 2 (bench).
The part mass is 1.0 kg and the gripper mass is 0.5 kg, so the payload is 1.5 kg.
The robot moves 2 moves per cycle, each taking 1.0 s, giving a cycle time of 2.0 s to meet 1800 parts per hour.
The robot approaches each point from above.
The fixtures are the conveyor for point 1 and the bench for point 2.
Please confirm that these values are correct.
